method: Reread Articles 4.1, 7.1 and 9.3 and reconstructed the term order from the dated programme scheme. Rechecked the relevant individual course entries before reassessing the frozen record and selected UCR evidence.
findings: The most commonly selected Greek/PThU route illustrates both biblical languages and the broad theology sequence. The three years each total 60 EC. The first-year Practical Theology and year-two Psychology and Sociology of Religion and Dogmatics are the formal PThU substitutions. Year three has 30 EC of specified PThU courses, one specialisation chosen in official order, seminar, science communication and thesis.

Phased Hebrew and Greek offerings satisfy the formal language gates. The current THB2-NT provides the New Testament and original cultural contexts ahead of the Greek-dependent exegesis unit. The controlling formal article names Turning Points in Christian Thought for Historical Theology, while the course description retains a Reformation-era title. Current Turning Points covers those thinkers and the dated programme places it before Historical Theology. Dogmatics is also earlier than both Historical and Intercultural Theology. The 60 EC year-two total meets the thesis gate before its 2b offering, after the seminar.

The UCR ethics route replaces the unavailable advanced-term sustainability research course with Climate Change. It retains introductory philosophy ahead of ethics, AI ethics, life-science and sustainability preparation and the later design course. The belief and public-life schedule remains feasible. Each option has 18 different courses and 135 EC not in the other.

The strongest alignments are philosophy of religion, interpretation of foundational narratives and ethical argument. The first route has a sustained cultural and institutional strand, while the second applies moral reasoning to scientific evidence and public problems. Biblical-language exegesis and professional spiritual or pastoral formation lack sustained depth at UCR. The record keeps the 10 EC Groningen thesis distinct from optional UCR research.

Reconciled the 24 external components, both UCR concepts, 42 selected course titles and descriptions, alignment rows, 11 audience note anchors and official links. Shared displayed descriptions were reused by matching their verified text and course name.
